title: Check performance and reliability
summary: Users leave slow or unreliable products. Agree how fast and available the product must be, test that it is, and make sure the team will know quickly when it is not.

beginner: Agree simple targets with engineers, for example 'pages load in under 2 seconds for most users' and 'the service is available 99.5 percent of the time'.
Find out how many users you expect at the busiest times.
Ask the team to test the product under that load and a bit more.
Check what happens when something fails: is there a clear error message and a way to recover?
Make sure alerts are set up so the team hears about problems before users complain.
intermediate: Agree service level objectives for speed and availability.
Run load and failure tests against expected peak use.
Check monitoring and alerting cover the key user journeys.
Decide what to fix before launch and what to accept.
experienced: Set objectives from the user's point of view and agree an error budget with engineering.
Use the error budget to balance new features against reliability work.
Plan capacity for growth and for unusual peaks.
Run game days to rehearse failures.

canDelegateTo.task: Set up monitoring, alerting and load tests
Run performance and failure test scenarios
Agree targets and decide on fixes

toolExamples.aws: Use CloudWatch alarms on error rates and response times for the key journeys.
toolExamples.azure: Use Azure Monitor alerts on error rates and response times.
toolExamples.gcp: Use Cloud Monitoring to set service level objectives and alerts.
toolExamples.vercel: Check Speed Insights for real-user page load times.

definitionOfDone: Monitoring and alerts cover key journeys
pitfalls: Testing only with a handful of users
No alerts, so users find problems first
Aiming for 100 percent availability, which is rarely worth the cost

leaderView.good: Speed and availability targets are tested before launch and watched afterwards.
ask: Have we tested at the load we expect on launch day?
What happens if this goes down?
signs: Performance is tested only on a developer's laptop.
There's no plan for peak demand.
